title: Rate Limiting
description: Learn how to protect Next.js APIs from abuse by limiting how many requests a client can make in a given time window using middleware and Redis.

data.text: Rate limiting restricts how many requests a client can send in a certain period. Without it, a single user, buggy script, or attacker can overwhelm your API, increase costs, or degrade performance for everyone else.

The two most common algorithms are fixed window and sliding window. Fixed window allows a set number of requests per minute or hour. Sliding window smooths out bursts by tracking requests over a rolling period.

items: Fixed window: 100 requests per minute, reset at the top of each minute
Sliding window: 100 requests in any rolling 60-second period
Token bucket: refill tokens over time, allow bursts up to a limit
Identify clients by IP, API key, or authenticated user ID

data.text: Rate limiting needs a fast shared store because your app may run on multiple servers. Redis is in-memory, supports atomic increment operations, and has built-in key expiration. It is the industry standard for this job.

data.title: Simple Redis rate limiter in Next.js middleware

data.text: IP-based limiting works for anonymous traffic, but logged-in users should have limits tied to their account. This prevents one user from exhausting the shared IP limit and also lets you offer different tiers.

data.title: Rate limiting by authenticated user ID
Tell Clients When They Can Retry
data.text: Return `Retry-After` headers with 429 responses so clients know how long to wait. Combine this with `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, and `X-RateLimit-Reset` headers for a polished API experience.

Limits depend on the cost of the endpoint. A cheap read-only endpoint can allow more requests than an endpoint that generates AI content or writes to a database. Start generous and tighten based on real usage and cost.

data.title: Key Takeaways
items: Rate limiting protects your API from abuse and cost overruns
Use Redis with a sliding window for accurate, fast limits
Limit by IP for anonymous users and by user ID for authenticated users
Return standard rate-limit headers so clients can adapt gracefully
